Encountered same issue. I tried to switch from env vars to file secrets, that are more secure and easy to manage in local PC environment. 

Unfortunately, current behavior severely breaks opencode UX and also CI and requires additional manual secret management.

Our team setup:
```
project-root
  - src/
  - .secrets/ # gitignored folder
  - opencode.json # references files from .secrets/
```

secret files are scoped per-profile, not global, because they may need per-worktree/branch/feature overrides

But when dealing with worktrees, after fresh worktree creation, opencode fails to start in this worktree unless .secrets/ are populated

This is even more painful in CI/CD when dev-facing MCPs that use those `{file:path}` secrets are not needed. This made our team to use split `opencode.json` and `opencode.ci.json`, and the only difference is that ci config skips MCP section

Also opencode web/desktop constantly shows "failed to load" warnings for all worktrees that have missing files. So eg I have open web UI in project's worktree worktr1 that has all proper secrets, but webui every N minutes (reload/polling time) spawns dozens of notifications "failed to load wrktr2", "failed to load wrktr3" and so on

I think that behavior when `{file:path}` syntax skips missing files and replaces it with `""` will be much more UX. It will match existing behavior of `{env:NAME}` syntax and prevent opencode from hard failures, which is especially important when working with web UI.
I also have this issue when working with GPT 5 Azure models

> Without OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL=true explicitly set when running opencode, the agent never tries to use LSP tools and always defaults to grep

The first issue i mentioned is definitely not part of those other existing issues

> With OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL=true, the agent tries to use LSP tools but always fails

The second issue does seem to have some overlap with https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29111 but not sure if it boils down to the same root cause as mine, so would like to keep open until the other one is resolved and we can verify the same issue doesn't exist for the workflow i described above

There's a second O(n^2) in the same `constructMessageRows` that's separate from the `groupParts` one @divitkashyap found: the `summary.diffs` dedup does `result.some()` inside `reduceRight` (message-timeline.data.ts ~L215). I hit a hang from a session with one message holding ~25k diffs (≈600M comparisons), nothing to do with part count.

Put up #30441 for just that line — Set-based dedup, O(n), same ordering semantics, with a 25k-entry regression test. It doesn't touch the parts/groupParts path, so it's complementary to the part-count circuit breaker discussed here.

Closing as related to #28844 (same `constructMessageRows` renderer hang). My fix targets a distinct O(n^2) path (the `summary.diffs` dedup) and is up as #30441, now linked to #28844. Consolidating there to avoid duplicate issues.

# Bug Report: App Crashes on Intel HD 4600 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT)

## Environment & Hardware

**Reproduced on:** Windows dual-GPU setup (Intel HD 4600 + NVIDIA GTX 1650)
**App Version:** 1.15.13

| GPU | Driver Version | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Intel HD Graphics 4600** | `20.19.15.4624` | **Crashes Electron renderer** |
| **NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650** | `32.0.15.6094` | Works fine |

---

## Behavior

* **Symptom:** App closes immediately upon launch.
* **Crash Sequence:** App launches → GPU process crashes → renderer crashes → EPIPE → app closes immediately.
* **Error Code:** `exit_code=-2147483645` (`0x80000003 STATUS_BREAKPOINT`)
* **Reproducibility:** 100% of the time with Intel HD 4600 enabled.

---

## Workarounds Tested

| Flag / Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `--disable-gpu` | ❌ Still crashes |
| `--use-gl=swiftshader` *(alone)* | ❌ Still crashes |
| `--disable-gpu-sandbox` | ❌ Still crashes |
| `--use-gl=swiftshader --in-process-gpu --disable-gpu-compositing` | Works (Temporary) |
| **Disabling Intel HD 4600** in Windows Device Manager | Works (Permanent) |

---

## Additional Context

* **Isolated Incident:** No other Electron apps are affected on this system (`Cursor`, `VS Code`, `Discord`, `Notion`, and `Claude` all work fine).
* **Unique Trigger:** OpenCode is the only app using `node-pty` + GPU compositing that triggers this specific crash.
* **CLI Version:** Works perfectly without issues.

---

## Suggestion

> **Add a "Disable Hardware Acceleration" toggle** in the application settings (similar to VS Code/Discord) as a user-facing fix for problematic or legacy GPU configurations.

Same issue. My contrib:

The bash tool executes any command the model writes, including destructive database operations like Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine). In a FastAPI+SQLAlchemy project, that can wipe the user's live local SQLite DB with no prompt, no undo, and no audit trail.

I lost ~2 hours of manually-entered data (1 cliente, 1 projeto, 2 tarefas, 4 apontamentos) when the model ran a one-off "spike" script to verify a Pydantic schema. 

The script imported the project's existing engine from app.core.database and called drop_all. The script was deleted immediately, but the data was already gone — no backup, no git history (data is in .db, not in source), no recovery path. Base.metadata.create_all re-created the empty schema on the next app start.

This is a guardrail gap, not a code bug. bash works exactly as designed; it just has no design for irreversibility. The model that did this to me had no mechanism to stop itself.

**Plugins**
None.

**OpenCode version**

Model: opencode/minimax-m3-free (MiniMax-M3) — but the bug is tool-level, not model-specific.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In a session whose project is a FastAPI app with a local SQLite dev DB (e.g. storage/app.db) and Base.metadata.create_all() on startup.
2. Ask the model to do "explore" or spike work that touches the schema.
3. The model writes a temp script spike.py that imports the existing engine from app.core.database and calls Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine).
4. Model runs it via bash. The import resolves to the live dev engine because that is the engine the app uses.
5. Model deletes the spike script. Dev DB is now empty schema + zero rows. User data is unrecoverable.

**Screenshot and/or share link**

Not applicable.

**Operating System**

Windows 11, working in PowerShell 5.1. Path has spaces (e.g. C:\dev\...\FreelaBoard\storage\freelaboard.db) — model used the existing engine object instead of any path string, so shell quoting was never the defense.

**Terminal**

Windows Terminal (PowerShell 5.1)

## Local reproduction evidence (v1.15.13, macOS Darwin)

Can confirm this bug with detailed local logs. Running OpenCode v1.15.13 on macOS (Darwin 25.4.0, zsh). Every crash session shows the same pattern: `oh-my-openagent` TUI plugin loads without a TUI entrypoint, then `setRawMode` fails within minutes.

### Crash pattern in non-pure mode

Four crash events captured in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/`, all following the identical sequence:

```
INFO  service=tui.plugin path=oh-my-openagent retry=false loading tui plugin
WARN  service=tui.plugin path=oh-my-openagent retry=false message=Plugin oh-my-openagent does not expose a tui entrypoint tui plugin has no entrypoint
... (1-8 minutes of normal operation) ...
ERROR service=default e=setRawMode failed with errno: 9 exception
ERROR service=default error=setRawMode failed with errno: 9 process error
ERROR service=default e=EIO: i/o error, write exception
INFO  service=default worker shutting down
INFO  service=default disposing all instances
```

**Crash timeline:**

| # | TUI log | Start time | Crash time | Uptime | Followed by EIO |
|---|---------|------------|------------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | `2026-06-01T224000` | 22:40:00 | 22:48:19 | 8m19s | Yes |
| 2 | `2026-06-01T224821` | 22:48:21 | 22:49:59 | 1m38s | No |
| 3 | `2026-06-01T225501` | 22:55:01 | 12:12:15 (next day) | ~13h | Yes |

Crashes #1 and #2 are a rapid double-crash — the first crash corrupts terminal state, and the second attempt fails within 94 seconds.

### `--pure` mode: zero errors

Tested with `opencode --pure` — the TUI log confirms all external plugins are skipped:

```
INFO  args=["--pure"]
INFO  service=tui.plugin count=1 skipping external tui plugins in pure mode
INFO  service=tui.plugin id=internal:home-footer loading internal tui plugin
... (internal plugins only, no oh-my-openagent) ...
```

The server log likewise shows:

```
INFO  service=plugin count=5 skipping external plugins in pure mode
```

**Result: zero `setRawMode` errors, zero `EIO` errors, stable session.**

### Root cause correlation

The `oh-my-openagent` plugin is loaded in every non-pure crash session but explicitly excluded in every stable `--pure` session. The `"does not expose a tui entrypoint"` warning appears immediately before the `setRawMode` failure in all three crash logs. This is consistent with the hypothesis that the plugin loading path in non-pure mode interferes with the TUI's TTY/raw-mode initialization.

### Environment

- **OpenCode**: v1.15.13
- **OS**: macOS Darwin 25.4.0
- **Shell**: zsh
- **Plugin**: `oh-my-openagent@latest` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
